scope_limits: The default typed recursion layout packs eight opening-reduction terms per row. The unchanged four-term minimum fusion threshold still recognizes short chains. All terms, authenticated lookups, start/end bindings and table-split rules are retained; inactive slots remain constrained.

The template identity includes the reduction terms per row and a new reduction-layout domain. This prevents reuse of old templates for the changed layout. The same constructor feeds CPU and GPU proof paths.

The hash layout remains two hashes per row. Quotient compiler emission and its instruction, source, register and private-memory caps are unchanged in the final source. The proposed four-hash specialization was profiled and reverted because of parent cost.

SmallTile admission additionally permits 32/64-column transforms, which shorter proof domains can select. Its kernels and local-memory geometry are unchanged. Independent analytic high-degree polynomial checks cover both widths, changed cosets, bit-reversed output and every element.

The comparison uses identical archived native inputs, proof counts, CPU worker policy, public-template cache policy and memory budgets from the previous accepted pass. Timings include CPU compilation/preparation, witness generation, GPU proving and CPU verification, but exclude OpenCL context initialization. This is a sequential component comparison, not a randomized ABBA experiment or confidence interval.

Driver caches were not cleared. The final comparison uses cached kernels; first-use compilation of the changed reduction kernel occurred in correctness testing. The rejected four-hash kernel took 124.39 seconds to compile on its first observed use, and that cost is retained in the rejected-candidate evidence.

CPU reference checks cover short and partial chains, every active/inactive term slot in the boundary fixture, accumulator shifts, two-table chain boundaries, next-row opening tampering and parent verifier bindings. Every measured proof is independently CPU verified; public and child-order mutations remain rejected.

No full fresh N3/N4 workflow or transaction-generation latency was measured. The primary screen covers twelve GBound leaves, the hierarchy covers eight singleton leaves and their parent, and the crypto screen covers a complete six-proof SHAKE request. These Linux OpenCL results do not qualify CUDA or macOS.

Security parameters, field arithmetic, hash rounds, transcript, randomness, query count and blowup are unchanged. Correctness checks for this layout do not replace the previously documented complete-tree soundness and zero-knowledge review.
